title: How Computers Represent Images · Level 1
slo: Explain how pixel values represent grayscale and RGB color images.

exercises.question_text: What do the letters RGB name?

options.text: Red, green, and blue
options.rationale: This is correct. RGB names the red, green, and blue channels.

options.text: Rows, grids, and boxes
options.error_type: confuses color channels with image dimensions
options.rationale: Rows and columns describe resolution. RGB names color hues.
options.better_fit: Use rows and columns when describing resolution.

feedback.intrinsic: Color layers would be confused with layout.
feedback.instructional: RGB stands for red, green, and blue.

options.text: Red, gray, and black
options.error_type: confuses RGB channels with grayscale values
options.rationale: Gray and black are grayscale shades. RGB includes green and blue.
options.better_fit: Use gray and black when describing grayscale values.

feedback.intrinsic: The color channels would be named incorrectly.
feedback.instructional: The channels are red, green, and blue.

options.text: Regions, gradients, and borders
options.error_type: confuses RGB channels with image features
options.rationale: These terms do not name color channels. RGB specifically names red, green, and blue.
options.better_fit: Use borders when discussing highlighted edges.

feedback.intrinsic: The color representation would be unclear.

exercises.explanation: Correct. RGB means red, green, and blue.

exercises.question_text: Which effects can filters create? Select all that apply.

options.text: Blurring an image
options.rationale: This is correct. Filters can blur by modifying pixel values.

options.text: Sharpening an image
options.rationale: This is correct. Sharpening is a filter effect.

options.text: Inverting colors
options.rationale: This is correct. Filters can invert pixel values to invert colors.

options.text: Adding RGB channels to every image
options.rationale: RGB channels describe color representation. A filter modifies existing values for an effect.
options.better_fit: Use RGB channels when describing color-image layers.

feedback.intrinsic: The format would be changed instead of applying an effect.
feedback.instructional: Filters can blur, sharpen, invert, or highlight edges.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Filters can blur, sharpen, and invert colors.

exercises.question_text: A typical RGB color image has separate pixel-value channels for red, green, and blue.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The color image would be described with the wrong layers.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: RGB means separate red, green, and blue channels.

exercises.explanation: Correct. RGB images use red, green, and blue value layers.

exercises.question_text: A filter changes an image by adding new pixel rows and columns to its resolution.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Image size would be changed rather than an effect applied.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Filtering manipulates pixel values; it does not define resolution.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Filters modify values, while resolution counts rows and columns.

exercises.question_text: Which facts describe a grayscale image? Select all that apply.

options.text: It has one layer of pixel values
options.rationale: This is correct. Grayscale uses a single pixel-value layer.

options.text: 0 can represent black
options.rationale: This is correct. In the stated range, 0 represents black.

options.text: It always uses red, green, and blue layers
options.rationale: RGB uses three color layers. Grayscale uses one value layer.
options.better_fit: Use this when describing a typical RGB image.

feedback.intrinsic: A grayscale image would be treated as color data.
feedback.instructional: Grayscale represents black, white, and gray with one layer.

options.text: Its resolution is always 255x255
options.error_type: confuses pixel value range with resolution
options.rationale: 255 is a possible intensity value. It is not a required image dimension.
options.better_fit: Use 255 for white in the stated grayscale range.

feedback.intrinsic: The dimensions would be reported incorrectly.
feedback.instructional: Keep pixel-value range separate from resolution.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Grayscale uses one layer, and 0 can represent black.

exercises.question_text: What does a 7x7 image resolution describe?

options.text: Seven pixel rows and seven columns
options.rationale: This is correct. Resolution describes an image by its pixel rows and columns.

options.text: Seven red, green, and blue layers
options.rationale: RGB layers describe color representation. They do not describe image dimensions.
options.better_fit: Use this for a typical RGB color image.

feedback.intrinsic: The dimensions would be recorded incorrectly.

options.text: Seven shades from black to white
options.rationale: Grayscale shades describe brightness values. They do not describe image size.
options.better_fit: Use this when discussing grayscale intensity.

feedback.intrinsic: The image size would remain unclear.
feedback.instructional: Resolution identifies pixel rows and columns.

options.text: Seven filter weights around each pixel
options.error_type: confuses image dimensions with a filter kernel
options.rationale: Kernel weights transform local pixels. They are not image resolution.
options.better_fit: Use this when discussing a filter kernel.

feedback.intrinsic: A filter property would replace the dimensions.
feedback.instructional: A 7x7 image has seven rows and seven columns.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Resolution gives the number of pixel rows and columns.

exercises.question_text: A grayscale image needs three channels for red, green, and blue.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The image would be described as color data.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Three channels belong to RGB images, not grayscale images.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Grayscale has one pixel-value layer.

exercises.question_text: A 7x7 image array contains 49 pixels because it has seven rows and seven columns.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The pixel count would be wrong.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Seven multiplied by seven gives 49 pixel positions.

exercises.question_text: What is padding used for during convolution near image edges?

options.text: Supply values where outside pixels are unavailable
options.rationale: This is correct. Padding supplies values, usually 0, beyond image edges.

options.text: Add color channels to a grayscale image
options.rationale: Color channels concern image representation. Padding handles unavailable outside pixels.
options.better_fit: Use RGB channels when describing a color image.

feedback.instructional: Padding fills positions beyond an image boundary.

options.text: Turn a kernel into a label prediction
options.rationale: Padding supports convolution at edges. It does not create labels or predictions.
options.better_fit: Use label prediction for image classification.

feedback.intrinsic: No edge values would be supplied.
feedback.instructional: Padding's purpose is handling unavailable outside pixels.

options.text: Make every pixel value equal to 255
options.rationale: 255 represents white in the stated grayscale range. Padding is usually 0 and applies around edges.
options.better_fit: Use 255 when representing white in grayscale.

feedback.intrinsic: The image would be incorrectly filled with white.
feedback.instructional: Padding is an edge treatment, usually using 0.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Padding supplies values where outside pixels are unavailable.

exercises.question_text: Which actions are part of convolution? Select all that apply.

options.text: Move a kernel across the image
options.rationale: This is correct. Convolution moves a kernel over local patches.

options.text: Multiply local pixels by matching weights
options.rationale: This is correct. Corresponding pixels and weights are multiplied.

options.text: Add the weighted results
options.rationale: This is correct. The products are added to form a weighted sum.

options.text: Replace pixels with RGB channel names
options.rationale: Convolution calculates numeric output values. RGB names color channels, not calculation steps.
options.better_fit: Use RGB names when describing a color image's layers.

feedback.intrinsic: Numeric calculations would be replaced by names.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Convolution uses a moving weighted-sum calculation.

exercises.question_text: A Laplace filter is used to blur an image by averaging nearby pixel values.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The intended object boundaries would not be emphasized.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: A Laplace filter highlights edges; blur is a different effect.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Laplace filtering highlights edges rather than blurring.

exercises.question_text: For each local patch, convolution multiplies pixel values by corresponding kernel weights and adds the results.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The output value would be calculated incorrectly.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Multiply matching pixels and weights, then add the products.

exercises.explanation: Correct. The weighted sum creates a transformed value.

flashcards.back: The number of pixel rows and columns in an image.
An image with one value layer for black, white, and gray shades.
Three pixel-value layers for red, green, and blue.
An array of weight values used to transform pixels.
